title.zh: 卷86 孝感:趙琰 長孫慮 乞伏保 孫益德 董洛生 楊引
title.en: Volume 86: Filial Piety - Zhao Yan, Zhang Sunlu, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin
title.raw: 卷86 孝感:趙琰 長孫慮 乞伏保 孫益德 董洛生 楊引 Volume 86: Filial Piety - Zhao Yan, Zhang Sunlu, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin

sentences.zh: 趙琰 長孫慮 乞伏保 孫益德 董洛生 楊引 閻元明 吳悉達 王續生 李顯達 張昇 倉跋 王崇 郭文恭

translations.literal: Zhao Yan, Zhangsun Lu, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Zhang Sheng, Cang Ba, Wang Chong, and Guo Wengong
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan, Zhangsun Lu, Qifu Bao, Sun Yide, Dong Luosheng, Yang Yin, Yan Yuanming, Wu Xida, Wang Xusheng, Li Xianda, Zhang Sheng, Cang Ba, Wang Chong, and Guo Wengong

sentences.zh: 經云「孝，德之本」，「孝悌之至，通於神明」。

translations.literal: The classics say, "Filial piety is the root of virtue," and "The utmost of filial piety and brotherly duty reaches through to the spirits."
translations.idiomatic: The classics say that filial piety is the root of virtue, and that the utmost filial piety and fraternal duty reach through to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 此蓋生人之大者。

translations.literal: This is perhaps the greatest matter for the living.
translations.idiomatic: This is surely among the greatest concerns of human life.

sentences.zh: 淳風既遠，世情雖薄，孔門有以責衣錦，詩人所以思素冠。

translations.literal: Though pure custom has long receded and worldly feeling has grown thin, Confucius's school had reason to rebuke returning home in brocade, and the poets therefore yearn for the plain cap.
translations.idiomatic: Pure custom has long since faded and worldly feeling has grown thin, yet Confucius's disciples had cause to reproach one who comes home in brocade, and the poets therefore pine for the plain mourning cap.

sentences.zh: 且生盡色養之天，終極哀思之地，若乃誠達泉魚，感通鳥獸，事匪常倫，斯蓋希矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, one has in life the heaven of fulfilling parental duty in their lifetime, and at the end the ground of deepest mourning; if sincerity reaches fish in the springs or moves birds and beasts, such matters are not ordinary norms—this is rare indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In life one has the span in which to serve parents with full devotion; at the end one reaches the ground of deepest mourning. When sincerity moves fish in the springs or touches birds and beasts, such things fall outside ordinary norms and are exceedingly rare.

sentences.zh: 至如溫床扇席，灌樹負土，時或加人，咸為度俗，今書趙琰等以孝感為目焉。

translations.literal: As for warming the bed and fanning the mat, watering trees and bearing earth on one's back—at times such conduct surpasses ordinary men, yet all serve to measure custom; this book takes Zhao Yan and the others and sets them under the rubric of filial response.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as warming the bed, fanning the mat, watering trees, and carrying earth on one's back sometimes surpass ordinary men, yet all serve to gauge custom. This book therefore treats Zhao Yan and the others under the heading of responsive filial piety.

sentences.zh: 趙琰，字叔起，天水人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yan, styled Shuq, was a man of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan, courtesy name Shuq, was from Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父溫為楊難當司馬。

translations.literal: His father Wen served as marshal to Yang Nanang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen served as marshal under Yang Nanang.

sentences.zh: 初，苻氏亂，琰為乳母攜奔壽春，年十四乃歸。

translations.literal: At first, during the Fu clan turmoil, Yan was taken in flight to Shouchun by his wet nurse and did not return until he was fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fu clan fell into chaos, Yan was carried off to Shouchun by his wet nurse and did not return until he was fourteen.

sentences.zh: 孝心色養，飪熟之節，必親調之。

translations.literal: In filial devotion he attended to his parents' comfort and appearance; at the season when food was cooked and done, he always seasoned it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents with filial devotion and attentive care for their comfort; whenever food was cooked and ready, he always seasoned it himself.

sentences.zh: 皇興中，京師儉，婢簡粟糶之，琰遇見切責，敕留輕粃。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, when the capital was straitened, a maid winnowed grain to sell; Yan chanced upon this and sternly rebuked her, ordering that only the light chaff be removed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangxing period, when the capital was in want, a servant winnowed grain to sell. Yan happened upon her and rebuked her sharply, ordering her to leave only the light chaff.

sentences.zh: 嘗送子應冀州娉室，從者於路偶得一羊，[2]行三十里而琰知之，令送於本處。

translations.literal: Once, when escorting his son Ying to fetch a bride in Jizhou, a follower on the road happened upon a sheep; after thirty li Yan learned of it and ordered it returned to where it had been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while escorting his son Ying to Jizhou to fetch a bride, a follower on the road happened to obtain a sheep. After they had gone thirty li Yan learned of it and ordered the sheep returned to its owner.

sentences.zh: 又過路傍，主人設羊羹，琰訪知盜殺，卒辭不食。

translations.literal: Again, passing a roadside host who set out mutton broth, Yan inquired and learned the animal had been stolen and killed; he thereupon declined and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he passed a roadside inn whose host served mutton broth. Yan learned the sheep had been stolen and slaughtered, and at once declined to eat.

sentences.zh: 遣人買耜刃，得剩六耜，即令送還刃主。

translations.literal: He sent someone to buy plowshares; receiving six extra shares, he at once had them returned to the share's owner.
translations.idiomatic: He sent someone to buy plowshares and received six extra shares in the bargain; he immediately had them returned to the owner.

sentences.zh: 刃主高之，義而不受，琰命委之而去。

translations.literal: The owner admired this and on principle would not accept them; Yan ordered them deposited and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The owner held him in esteem and on principle refused to take them back; Yan ordered the shares left with him and departed.

sentences.zh: 初為兗州司馬，轉團城鎮副將。

translations.literal: At first he was marshal of Yanzhou, then transferred to deputy commandant of Tuncheng garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as marshal of Yanzhou, then was transferred to deputy commandant of Tuncheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 還京，為淮南王他府長史。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he became chief clerk in the household of the Prince of Huainan, Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he became chief clerk in the household of Prince Huainan Tuo.

sentences.zh: 時禁制甚嚴，不聽越關葬於舊兆。

translations.literal: At that time prohibitions were very strict; crossing the frontier to bury at the old tombs was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time restrictions were very strict, and burial at the old family tombs across the frontier was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 琰積三十餘年，不得葬二親。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years Yan could not bury his two parents.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years Yan could not bury his two parents.

sentences.zh: 及蒸嘗拜獻，未曾不嬰慕卒事。

translations.literal: At seasonal offerings and sacrifices he never failed, when the rites were completed, to be seized by longing and grief.
translations.idiomatic: At every seasonal offering and sacrifice, when the rites were finished he was never free of overwhelming grief.

sentences.zh: 每於時節，不受子孫慶賀。

translations.literal: At each festival he would not accept congratulations from his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: At each festival season he would not accept congratulations from his descendants.

sentences.zh: 年餘耳順，而孝思彌篤。

translations.literal: Though he was past sixty, his thoughts of filial piety grew only more earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Though he was past sixty, his filial thoughts grew only more earnest.

sentences.zh: 慨歲月推移，遷窆無期，乃絕鹽粟，斷諸滋味，食麥而已。

translations.literal: Lamenting the passage of years and that moving the coffins had no fixed date, he gave up salt and grain, cut off all flavorings, and ate only wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Lamenting the passage of years and that reinterment had no fixed date, he gave up salt and grain, cut off all other flavors, and ate only wheat.

sentences.zh: 年八十卒。

translations.literal: He died at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 遷都洛陽，遷都洛陽，子應等乃還鄉葬焉。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, when the capital was moved to Luoyang, Ying and the others were finally able to return home and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, Ying and his brothers were at last able to return home and bury their parents.

sentences.zh: 應弟煦，字賓育。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Xu, styled Binyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Xu, courtesy name Binyu.

sentences.zh: 好音律，以善歌聞於世。

translations.literal: He loved music and was famed throughout the world for fine singing.
translations.idiomatic: He loved music and was renowned throughout the realm for his fine singing.

sentences.zh: 位秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the post of governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 長孫慮，代人也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Lu, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lu was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 母因飲酒，其父真呵叱之，誤以杖擊，便即致死。

translations.literal: His mother, having taken drink, was scolded by his father Zhen; he mistakenly struck her with his staff and at once caused her death.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been drinking when his father Zhen scolded her; he mistakenly struck her with his staff and killed her on the spot.

sentences.zh: 真為縣囚執，處以重坐。

translations.literal: Zhen was seized as a county prisoner and sentenced to a heavy penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was seized as a county prisoner and sentenced to a heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 慮列辭尚書云：「父母忿爭，本無餘惡。

translations.literal: Lu submitted a memorial to the Ministry of Works, saying: "When parents quarrel in anger, there is originally no deep malice.
translations.idiomatic: Lu submitted a petition to the Ministry of Works, saying: "When parents quarrel in anger, there is originally no deep malice.

sentences.zh: 直以謬誤，一朝橫禍。

translations.literal: It was only through a blunder that calamity struck in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: It was only through a mistake that disaster struck in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 今母喪未殯，父命旦夕。

translations.literal: Now my mother's funeral is not yet prepared for burial, and my father's life hangs by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: Now my mother's body lies unburied, and my father's life hangs by a thread.

sentences.zh: 慮兄弟五人，並各幼稚。

translations.literal: Lu and his five brothers are each still young.
translations.idiomatic: Lu and his five brothers are each still young.

sentences.zh: 慮身居長，今年十五，有一女弟，始向四歲，更相鞠養，不能保全。

translations.literal: I, Lu, am the eldest, fifteen this year, with one younger sister just turning four; if we must rear one another, we cannot keep everyone safe.
translations.idiomatic: I, Lu, am the eldest, fifteen this year, with one younger sister who has just turned four. If we must raise one another, we cannot keep everyone alive.

sentences.zh: 父若就刑，交墜溝壑，乞以身代老父命，使嬰弱眾孤得蒙存立。」

translations.literal: If my father goes to execution, we will all fall into ditches and gullies; I beg to take my aged father's place in death, so that the infants and the many orphans may be granted survival.
translations.idiomatic: If my father goes to execution, we will all fall into ditches and ravines. I beg to die in my aged father's place, so that the infants and many orphans may be allowed to live.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏云：「慮於父為孝子，於弟為仁兄。

translations.literal: The Ministry reported: "Lu is a filial son toward his father and a benevolent elder brother toward his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reported: "Lu is a filial son toward his father and a benevolent elder brother toward his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 尋究情狀，特可矜感。」

translations.literal: Examining the circumstances, he is especially deserving of pity and sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: On examining the circumstances, he is especially deserving of pity and compassion.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔特恕其父死罪，以從遠流。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu decreed that his father's capital crime be specially pardoned and commuted to exile to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu decreed that his father's capital crime be specially pardoned and commuted to exile in a distant region.

sentences.zh: 乞伏保，高車部人也。

translations.literal: Qifu Bao, a man of the Gaoche tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Bao was a man of the Gaoche tribes.

sentences.zh: 父居，顯祖時為散騎常侍，領牧曹尚書，賜爵寧國侯。

translations.literal: His father Ju, in Emperor Xianzu's time was Regular Attendant, head of the Pasturage and Herds Office of the Ministry, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju, in Emperor Xianzu's reign, was Regular Attendant and head of the Pasturage and Herds Office of the Ministry, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ning.

sentences.zh: 以忠謹慎密，常在左右，出內詔命。

translations.literal: Because of loyalty, prudence, and discretion he was always at the emperor's side, issuing all edicts inward and outward.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his loyalty, prudence, and discretion he was always at the emperor's side, conveying all edicts within and without.

sentences.zh: 賜宮人河南宗氏，亡後，賜以宮人申氏，宋太子左率申坦兄女也。

translations.literal: He was granted the palace woman Zong of Henan; after her death he was granted the palace woman Shen, daughter of Shen Tan, elder brother of the Song heir apparent's Left Leader.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the palace woman Zong of Henan. After her death he was granted the palace woman Shen, daughter of Shen Tan, elder brother of the Song heir apparent's Left Leader.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，居卒，申撫養伏保。

translations.literal: After a year and more Ju died; Shen reared and nurtured Bao.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year Ju died, and Shen reared and nurtured Bao.

sentences.zh: 性嚴肅，捶罵切至，而伏保奉事孝謹，初無恨色。

translations.literal: She was severe and beat and scolded him harshly, yet Bao served her with filial care and at first showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: She was stern and beat and scolded him harshly, yet Bao served her with filial care and at first showed no resentment.

sentences.zh: 襲父侯爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's marquisate, which by rule was reduced to a barony.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's marquisate, which by regulation was reduced to a barony.

sentences.zh: 稍遷左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Left Palace Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Left Palace Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 每請祿賜，在外公私尺丈所用，無不白知。

translations.literal: Whenever he requested salary or gifts, every foot and yard of cloth used in public or private outside the household was reported to her without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he requested salary or gifts, every measure of cloth used in public or private affairs outside the household was reported to her without exception.

sentences.zh: 出為鄯善鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out as commandant of Shanshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as commandant of Shanshan garrison.

sentences.zh: [3]申年餘八十，伏保手製馬輿，親自扶接，申欣然隨之。

translations.literal: When Shen was past eighty, Bao personally made a horse carriage and supported and accompanied her himself; Shen went along gladly.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen was past eighty, Bao personally made a horse carriage and supported and accompanied her himself; Shen went along gladly.

sentences.zh: 申亡，伏保解官，奉喪還洛。

translations.literal: When Shen died, Bao resigned his post and conveyed the coffin back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen died, Bao resigned his office and conveyed the coffin back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 復為長，兼南中郎將，卒。

translations.literal: Later he again served as Chief, also concurrently Southern Palace General, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again served as Chief and concurrently as Southern Palace General, and died.

sentences.zh: 孫益德，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yide, a man of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yide was a man of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 其母為人所害，益德童幼為母復仇。

translations.literal: His mother had been killed by someone; while still a child Yide avenged his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been killed by someone; while still a child Yide avenged her.

sentences.zh: 還家，哭於殯以待縣官。

translations.literal: Returning home, he wept beside the coffin awaiting the district authorities.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home and wept beside the coffin, awaiting the district authorities.

sentences.zh: 高祖、文明太后以其幼而孝決。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming judged him filial though young.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming judged him filial though young.

sentences.zh: 又不逃罪，特免之。

translations.literal: Moreover, he had not fled punishment, so they specially exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he had not fled punishment, so they specially exempted him.

sentences.zh: 董洛生，代人也。

translations.literal: Dong Luosheng, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Luosheng was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 居父喪過禮，詔遣祕書中散溫紹伯奉璽書慰之，令自抑割以全孝道。

translations.literal: Dwelling in mourning for his father beyond the rites, an edict sent Secretariat Attendant Wen Shaobo with the imperial seal-letter to console him, ordering him to restrain himself so as to preserve full filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning for his father beyond the proper rites. An edict sent Secretariat Attendant Wen Shaobo with the imperial seal-letter to console him, ordering him to restrain his grief so as to preserve his filial duty intact.

sentences.zh: 又詔其宗親，使相喻奬，勿令有滅性之譏。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered his kinsmen to exhort and encourage one another, that he should not earn reproach for destroying his own life.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered his kinsmen to exhort and encourage him, lest he earn reproach for destroying his own life.

sentences.zh: 楊引，鄉郡襄垣人也。

translations.literal: Yang Yin, a man of Xiangyuan in Xiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin was a man of Xiangyuan in Xiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 三歲喪父，為叔所養。

translations.literal: At three he lost his father and was reared by his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of three he lost his father and was reared by his uncle.

sentences.zh: 母年九十三卒，引年七十五，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: His mother died at ninety-three; Yin was seventy-five and his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at ninety-three; Yin was seventy-five, and his grief and emaciation exceeded the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 三年服畢，恨不識父，追服斬衰，食粥粗服，誓終身命。

translations.literal: When the three-year mourning was complete, grieving that he had never known his father, he put on the coarsest hemp mourning, ate only gruel in rough clothes, and vowed for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When the three-year mourning for his mother was complete, grieving that he had never known his father, he put on the coarsest hemp mourning, ate only gruel in rough clothes, and vowed to keep this for life.

sentences.zh: 終十三年，哀慕不改，為郡縣鄉閭三百餘人上狀稱美。

translations.literal: For a full thirteen years his longing did not change; more than three hundred people of the district, county, and village submitted memorials praising him.
translations.idiomatic: For a full thirteen years his longing did not change. More than three hundred people of the district, county, and village submitted memorials praising him.

sentences.zh: 有司奏宜旌賞，復其一門，樹其純孝。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that he should be honored and rewarded, restoring corvée for his whole household and setting up his pure filial piety as an example.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized that he should be honored and rewarded, restoring corvée for his entire household and holding up his pure filial piety as an example.

sentences.zh: 詔別敕集書標楊引至行，又可假以散員之名。

translations.literal: An edict separately ordered the Secretariat to mark Yin's supreme conduct, and he might also be given the name of a supernumerary official.
translations.idiomatic: An edict separately ordered the Secretariat to mark Yin's supreme conduct, and he might also be granted the title of a supernumerary official.

sentences.zh: 閻元明，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Yan Yuanming, a man of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yuanming was a man of Anyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少而至孝，行著鄉閭。

translations.literal: From youth he was supremely filial, his conduct renowned in village and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was supremely filial, and his conduct was renowned throughout his village and hamlet.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，除北隨郡太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was appointed governor of North Suiguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Taihe era he was appointed governor of North Suiguan.

sentences.zh: 元明以違離親養，興言悲慕，母亦慈念，泣淚喪明。

translations.literal: Yuanming, having left his parents' support, spoke with grief and longing; his mother too thought on him with tenderness, weeping until she lost her sight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming, having left his parents' support, spoke with grief and longing. His mother too cherished him in her thoughts and wept until she lost her sight.

sentences.zh: 元明悲號上訴，許歸奉養。

translations.literal: Yuanming wailed and appealed upward; he was permitted to return and tend them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanming wailed and appealed to the authorities; he was permitted to return and support his parents.

sentences.zh: 一見其母，母目便開。

translations.literal: At first sight of his mother, her eyes opened at once.
translations.idiomatic: At his first sight of his mother, her eyes opened at once.

sentences.zh: 刺史呂壽恩列狀上聞，詔下州郡，表為孝門，復其租調兵役，令終母年。

translations.literal: Prefect Lü Shou'en submitted a report to the throne; an edict went down to the provinces and commanderies, marking his household as a Gate of Filial Piety, restoring rent and corvée, and granting him leave until his mother's years were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Lü Shou'en submitted a report to the throne. An edict went down to the provinces and commanderies, marking his household as a Gate of Filial Piety, restoring his rent and corvée obligations, and granting him leave until his mother's lifetime was complete.

sentences.zh: 母亡，服終，心喪積載，每忌日悲慟傍隣。

translations.literal: When his mother died and mourning was complete, his inner mourning lasted many years; on each anniversary of her death his laments moved the neighbors beside him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and the mourning period was complete, his inner mourning lasted many years. On each anniversary of her death his laments moved the neighbors beside him.

sentences.zh: 昆弟雍和，尊卑諧穆，安貧樂道，白首同歸。

translations.literal: Brothers were harmonious, elders and juniors in concord, content in poverty and devoted to the Way, white-haired together to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were harmonious, elders and juniors in concord, content in poverty and devoted to the Way, growing white-haired together to the end.

sentences.zh: 又猗氏縣人令狐仕，兄弟四人，早喪父，泣慕十載，奉養其母，孝著鄉邑。

translations.literal: Also Linghu Shi of Yishi county—the four brothers lost their father early, wept and longed for ten years, supported their mother, and were noted for filial piety in village and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Also Linghu Shi of Yishi county: the four brothers lost their father early, wept and longed for ten years, supported their mother, and were noted for filial piety throughout village and hamlet.

sentences.zh: 而力田積粟，博施不已。

translations.literal: Yet they plowed fields and stored grain, giving generously without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they plowed fields and stored grain, giving generously without cease.

sentences.zh: 又河東郡人楊風等七百五十人，列稱樂戶皇甫奴兄弟，雖沉屈兵伍而操尚彌高，奉養繼親甚著恭孝之稱。

translations.literal: Also Yang Feng and seven hundred fifty others of Hedong commandery submitted jointly that the music-household brothers Huangfu Nu and his siblings, though sunken and bent in the ranks of soldiers, were yet of loftier conduct, rearing their stepmother with utmost respectful filial fame.
translations.idiomatic: Also Yang Feng and seven hundred fifty others of Hedong commandery submitted jointly that the music-household brothers Huangfu Nu and his siblings, though sunk in the ranks of soldiers, were yet of loftier conduct, rearing their stepmother with the utmost reputation for respectful filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又東郡小黃縣人董吐渾、兄養，事親至孝，三世同居，閨門有禮。

translations.literal: Also Dong Tuhun and his elder brother Yang of Xiaohuang in Dongjun—serving their parents with utmost filial piety, three generations dwelling together, the inner quarters ordered by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Also Dong Tuhun and his elder brother Yang of Xiaohuang in Dongjun served their parents with utmost filial piety. Three generations dwelt together, and the inner quarters were ordered by ritual.

sentences.zh: 景明初，畿內大使王凝奏請標異，詔從之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, metropolitan envoy Wang Ning memorialized asking that they be marked out; an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era, metropolitan envoy Wang Ning memorialized asking that they be marked out for distinction; an edict followed his request.

sentences.zh: 吳悉達，河東聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Wu Xida, a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xida was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 弟兄三人，年並幼小，父母為人所殺，四時號慕，悲感鄉隣。

translations.literal: Three brothers, all still young—their parents were killed by others; through the four seasons they called out in longing, their grief moving village and neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: Three brothers, all still young: their parents were killed by others. Through the four seasons they called out in longing, and their grief moved village and neighbor.

sentences.zh: 及長報仇，避地永安。

translations.literal: When grown they took revenge and fled to Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: When they grew up they took revenge and fled to Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 昆弟同居四十餘載，閨門和睦，讓逸競勞。

translations.literal: The brothers dwelt together more than forty years; inner quarters were harmonious, yielding and deferring, competing only in labor.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers dwelt together for more than forty years. Their household was harmonious; they yielded and deferred to one another, competing only in labor.

sentences.zh: 雖於儉年糊饘不繼，賓客經過，必傾所有。

translations.literal: Even in lean years when thin gruel barely held together, whenever guests passed by they would pour out all they had.
translations.idiomatic: Even in lean years when thin gruel barely held together, whenever guests passed by they would pour out all they had.

sentences.zh: 每守宰殯喪，私辦車牛，送終葬所。

translations.literal: Whenever a magistrate or prefect had a funeral, they privately provided carts and oxen for the journey to the burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a magistrate or prefect had a funeral, they privately provided carts and oxen to convey the coffin to the burial ground.

sentences.zh: 隣人孤貧窘困者，莫不解衣輟糧以相賑恤。

translations.literal: For neighbors who were orphaned, poor, or in hardship, there was none who did not strip off clothing or grain to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: For neighbors who were orphaned, poor, or in hardship, there was none who did not strip off clothing or set aside grain to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 鄉閭五百餘人詣州稱頌焉。

translations.literal: More than five hundred people of village and hamlet went to the prefecture to acclaim them.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred people of village and hamlet went to the prefecture to acclaim them.

sentences.zh: 刺史以悉達兄弟行著鄉里，板贈悉達父勃海太守。

translations.literal: The prefect, because the Xida brothers' conduct shone in their locale, by plaque posthumously granted Xida's father the title of Governor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect, because the Xida brothers' conduct shone in their locale, by plaque posthumously granted Xida's father the title of Governor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 悉達後欲改葬，亡失墳墓，推尋弗獲，號哭之聲晝夜不止，叫訴神祇。

translations.literal: Later Xida wished to rebury them but had lost the grave; searching he could not find it. His cries day and night did not cease as he appealed to the gods.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xida wished to rebury them but had lost the grave. Though he searched he could not find it. His cries day and night did not cease as he appealed to the spirits.

sentences.zh: 忽於悉達足下地陷，得父銘記。

translations.literal: Suddenly the ground beneath Xida's feet sank, and he recovered his father's inscribed marker.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the ground beneath Xida's feet sank, and he recovered his father's inscribed grave marker.

sentences.zh: 因遷葬曾祖已下三世九喪，傾盡資業，不假於人，哀感毀悴，有過初喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved the graves of three generations, nine coffins from his great-grandfather down, exhausting his family's resources without borrowing from others; his grief and wasting surpassed even the first mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he moved the graves of three generations—nine coffins from his great-grandfather down—exhausting his family's resources without borrowing from others. His grief and emaciation surpassed even the first mourning.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，標閭復役，以彰孝義。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported to the throne; his village was marked out and corvée restored, to manifest filial righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported to the throne. His village was marked out for distinction and corvée restored, to manifest filial righteousness.

sentences.zh: 時有齊州人崔承宗，其父於宋世仕漢中，母喪，因殯彼。

translations.literal: At that time there was Cui Chengzong of Qizhou; his father had served in Hanzhong under the Song, and when his mother died was buried there.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Cui Chengzong of Qizhou. His father had served in Hanzhong under the Song, and when his mother died she was buried there.

sentences.zh: 後青徐歸國，遂為隔絕。

translations.literal: Later when Qing and Xu returned to the realm, they were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qing and Xu returned to the [Northern Wei] realm, they were cut off from one another.

sentences.zh: 承宗性至孝，萬里投險，偷路負喪還京師。

translations.literal: Chengzong was by nature supremely filial; casting himself into danger across ten thousand li, he stole along the road carrying the coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong was by nature supremely filial. Casting himself into danger across ten thousand li, he stole along the road carrying the coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎孫惠蔚聞之曰：「吾於斯人見廉范之情矣。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said: "In this man I see the sentiment of Lian Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Sun Huiwei heard of it and said: "In this man I see the devotion of Lian Fan.

sentences.zh: 於是弔贈盡禮，如舊相識。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent condolences and gifts with full rites, as with an old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent condolences and gifts with full ceremony, as with an old acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 王續生，滎陽京縣人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xusheng was a man of Jing county in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xusheng was from Jing county in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 遭繼母憂，居喪杖而後起。

translations.literal: He suffered mourning for his stepmother and dwelt in mourning, leaning on a staff before he could rise.
translations.idiomatic: When his stepmother died he observed mourning, leaning on a staff before he could rise.

sentences.zh: 及終禮制，鬢髮盡落。

translations.literal: When the mourning rites were complete, his temples and hair all fell out.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning rites were complete, all his hair fell out.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，世宗詔標旌門閭，甄其徭役。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported to the throne; Emperor Shizong decreed to mark his gate and hamlet and exempt him from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported to the throne. Emperor Shizong decreed that his gate and hamlet be marked and his corvée obligations waived.

sentences.zh: 李顯達，潁川陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Li Xianda was a man of Yangzhai in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianda was from Yangzhai in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父喪，水漿不入口七日，鬢髮墮落，形體枯悴。

translations.literal: At his father's death he took no broth for seven days; his temples and hair fell, and his form was wasted and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he took no broth for seven days. His hair fell out and his body wasted away.

sentences.zh: 六年廬於墓側，哭不絕聲，殆於滅性。

translations.literal: For six years he built a hut by the tomb; his weeping never ceased, nearly destroying his own life.
translations.idiomatic: For six years he built a hut beside the tomb and wept without cease, nearly destroying his own life.

sentences.zh: 州牧、高陽王雍以狀奏，靈太后詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: Regional governor Prince Yong of Gaoyang submitted the report; Empress Dowager Ling decreed to mark his gate and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Regional governor Prince Yong of Gaoyang submitted a report. Empress Dowager Ling decreed that his gate and hamlet be marked.

sentences.zh: 張昇，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng was a man of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng was a man of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 居父母喪，鬢髮墜落，水漿不入口，吐血數升。

translations.literal: Dwelling in mourning for both parents, his temples and hair fell; he took no broth and spat blood by the several sheng.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning both parents, his hair fell out. He took no broth and spat several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 詔表門閭。

translations.literal: An edict marked his gate and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: An edict marked his gate and hamlet.

sentences.zh: 倉跋，滎陽京縣人也。

translations.literal: Cang Ba was a man of Jing county in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cang Ba was from Jing county in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 喪母，水漿不入口五日，吐血數升，居憂毀瘠，見稱州里。

translations.literal: At his mother's death he took no broth for five days, spat blood by the several sheng, and in mourning was wasted and emaciated—acclaimed in his district and village.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he took no broth for five days and spat several sheng of blood. In mourning he was wasted and emaciated, and was acclaimed throughout his district and village.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，出帝詔標門閭。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported to the throne; Emperor Chu decreed to mark his gate and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported to the throne. Emperor Chu decreed that his gate and hamlet be marked.

sentences.zh: 王崇，字乾邕，陽夏雍丘人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chong, styled Qianyong, was a man of Yongqiu in Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong, courtesy name Qianyong, was from Yongqiu in Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並以孝稱。

translations.literal: The brothers were all famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 身勤稼穡，以養二親。

translations.literal: He himself labored in the fields and sowed grain to support his two parents.
translations.idiomatic: He himself labored in the fields and sowed grain to support his two parents.

sentences.zh: 仕梁州鎮南府主簿。

translations.literal: He served as chief clerk of the Southern Headquarters of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk of the Southern Headquarters of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 母亡，杖而後起，鬢髮墮落。

translations.literal: When his mother died he leaned on a staff before he could rise, and his temples and hair fell.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he leaned on a staff before he could rise, and his hair fell out.

sentences.zh: 未及葬，權殯宅西。

translations.literal: Before burial was complete, the coffin was temporarily lodged west of the house.
translations.idiomatic: Before burial could be completed, the coffin was temporarily lodged west of the house.

sentences.zh: 崇廬於殯所，晝夜哭泣，鳩鴿羣至。

translations.literal: Chong built a hut at the mourning site and wept day and night; doves and pigeons gathered in flocks.
translations.idiomatic: Chong built a hut at the mourning site and wept day and night. Doves and pigeons gathered in flocks.

sentences.zh: 有一小鳥，素質墨眸，形大如雀，栖於崇廬，朝夕不去。

translations.literal: There was a small bird, plain in color with black pupils, the size of a sparrow; it perched on Chong's hut and did not leave morning or evening.
translations.idiomatic: A small bird, plain in color with black eyes, as large as a sparrow, perched on Chong's hut and did not leave from morning to evening.

sentences.zh: 母喪始闋，復丁父憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother had just ended, he again suffered his father's mourning; his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his mother had just ended, he again mourned his father. His grief and emaciation exceeded the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 是年，陽夏風雹，所過之處，禽獸暴死，草木摧折。

translations.literal: That year in Yangxia there was wind and hail; wherever it passed, birds and beasts died violently and plants were broken.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yangxia was struck by wind and hail. Wherever it passed, birds and beasts died and plants were broken.

sentences.zh: 至崇田畔，風雹便止，禾麥十頃，竟無損落，及過崇地，風雹如初。

translations.literal: When it reached Chong's field the wind and hail stopped; ten qing of grain and wheat were wholly undamaged—and when it passed Chong's ground the hail resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: When it reached Chong's field the wind and hail stopped. Ten qing of grain and wheat were wholly undamaged. Once it had passed beyond Chong's land, the hail resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 咸稱至行所感。

translations.literal: All said it was moved by his supreme conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All said this was a response to his supreme conduct.

sentences.zh: 崇雖除服，仍居墓側。

translations.literal: Though Chong had doffed mourning garments, he still dwelt beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chong had doffed mourning garments, he still dwelt beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 於其室前生草一根，莖葉甚茂，人莫能識。

translations.literal: Before his chamber a single blade of grass sprang up, stem and leaves very lush, and none could name it.
translations.idiomatic: Before his chamber a single blade of grass sprang up, its stem and leaves very lush, and no one could identify it.

sentences.zh: 至冬中，復有烏巢於崇屋，乳養三子，毛羽成長，馴而不驚。

translations.literal: In mid-winter again crows nested on Chong's roof, suckling and rearing three young; when their feathers were full grown they were tame and not startled.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-winter crows again nested on Chong's roof, suckling and rearing three young. When their feathers were full grown they were tame and not startled.

sentences.zh: 守令聞之，親自臨視。

translations.literal: The magistrate and prefect heard of it and came in person to view it.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate and prefect heard of it and came in person to observe.

sentences.zh: 州以聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The province reported to the throne; his gate and hamlet were marked.
translations.idiomatic: The province reported to the throne, and his gate and hamlet were marked.

sentences.zh: 郭文恭，太原平遙人也。

translations.literal: Guo Wengong was a man of Pingyao in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wengong was from Pingyao in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 仕為太平縣令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Taiping county.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Taiping county.

sentences.zh: 年踰七十，父母喪亡。

translations.literal: Past seventy years, his parents died.
translations.idiomatic: After he had passed seventy, his parents died.

sentences.zh: 文恭孝慕罔極，乃居祖父墓次，晨夕拜跪。

translations.literal: Wengong's filial longing was boundless; he therefore dwelt beside his grandfather's tomb, bowing and kneeling morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Wengong's filial longing was boundless. He therefore dwelt beside his grandfather's tomb, bowing and kneeling morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 跣足負土，培祖父二墓，寒暑竭力，積年不已，見者莫不哀歎。

translations.literal: Barefoot he bore earth and banked up his grandfather's two tombs; through cold and heat he strained with all his strength year on year without cease—those who saw it none failed to sigh in pity.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot he bore earth and banked up his grandfather's two tombs. Through cold and heat he strained with all his strength year after year without cease. None who saw it failed to sigh in pity.

sentences.zh: 尚書聞奏，標其門閭。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works heard and reported; his gate and hamlet were marked.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works heard and reported to the throne. His gate and hamlet were marked.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：塞天地而橫四海者，唯孝而已矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: He who blocks heaven and earth and spans the four seas is filial piety alone.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Only filial piety can fill heaven and earth and span the four seas.

sentences.zh: 然則始敦孝敬之方，終極哀思之道，厥亦多緒，其心一焉。

translations.literal: Thus from first cultivating the method of respect and devotion to reaching the path of utmost mourning thought—though these have many threads, the heart is one.
translations.idiomatic: From first cultivating respect and devotion to reaching the utmost path of mourning—though these have many strands, the heart is one.

sentences.zh: 蓋上智禀自然之質，中庸有企及之義，及其成名，其美一也。

translations.literal: The highest wisdom is endowed with nature's substance; the middling have the principle of striving to reach—and when they achieve fame, their beauty is one.
translations.idiomatic: The highest wisdom is endowed with nature's substance; the middling possess the resolve to strive toward it—and when they achieve renown, their excellence is one.

sentences.zh: 趙琰等或出公卿之緒，籍禮教以資；

translations.literal: Zhao Yan and others either issued from the line of duke and minister, drawing support from ritual teaching;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan and others either issued from lines of dukes and ministers, drawing support from ritual teaching;

sentences.zh: 或出茅簷之下，非奬勸所得。

translations.literal: or came from beneath thatched eaves, not obtained by reward and exhortation.
translations.idiomatic: or came from beneath thatched eaves, not won through reward and exhortation.

sentences.zh: 乃有負土成墳，致毀滅性，雖乖先王之典制，亦觀過而知仁矣。

translations.literal: Some bore earth until tombs were mounds and brought ruin on their own lives; though this departs from the former kings' regulations, one may yet observe the fault and know the benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Some bore earth until tombs were mounds and brought ruin on their own lives. Though this departs from the former kings' regulations, one may yet observe the excess and recognize the benevolence within it.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十六 諸本目錄注「闕」。

translations.literal: In all editions of the Book of Wei, juan 86, the table of contents is marked "missing."
translations.idiomatic: In all editions of the Book of Wei, juan 86, the table of contents is marked "missing."

sentences.zh: 卷末有宋人校語

translations.literal: At the end of the juan is a Song-dynasty collation note
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the juan there is a Song-dynasty collation note

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Palace Edition entered into textual verification〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Palace Edition entered into textual verification〉

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書孝感傳亡，惟張昇事出宗諫史目，與北史小異，高氏小史不載昇事迹。

translations.literal: It says: "Wei Shou's book's Filial Response Biography is lost; only Zhang Sheng's affair comes from Zong Jian's historiographical catalogue, differing slightly from the History of the Northern Dynasties; Gao's Brief History does not record Sheng's deeds.
translations.idiomatic: It says: "Wei Shou's Filial Response biography is lost. Only Zhang Sheng's account comes from Zong Jian's historiographical catalogue, differing slightly from the History of the Northern Dynasties. Gao's Brief History does not record Sheng's deeds.

sentences.zh: 案小史孝感、節義、良吏、列女、閹官五傳敍目並傳，與正史及諸書目次序前後不同，惟楊九齡經史目錄與小史同。

translations.literal: It is considered that the Brief History's five biographies—Filial Response, Chastity and Righteousness, Good Officials, Exemplary Women, and Eunuch Officials—have prefaces and texts together, their order before and after differing from the official histories and various catalogues; only Yang Jiuling's Classified Catalogue of Classics and Histories agrees with the Brief History.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief History's five biographies—Filial Response, Chastity and Righteousness, Good Officials, Exemplary Women, and Eunuch Officials—have prefaces and texts together, but their order differs from the official histories and various catalogues. Only Yang Jiuling's Classified Catalogue of Classics and Histories agrees with the Brief History.

sentences.zh: 九齡撰錄皆在殷仲藏、宗諫等後，是時正史已不完，往往取小史為據，故同之。」

translations.literal: Jiuling's compilation all comes after Yin Zhongcang, Zong Jian, and others; by then the official history was already incomplete and often took the Brief History as authority, hence the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling's compilation all comes after Yin Zhongcang, Zong Jian, and others. By then the official history was already incomplete, and compilers often took the Brief History as their authority—hence the agreement.

sentences.zh: 按此傳序與北史卷八四孝行傳序不同，諸傳只張昇傳出宗諫史目，見上宋人校語，他傳全同北史，論也出北史，而稍有刪節。

translations.literal: This biography's preface differs from the History of the Northern Dynasties juan 84 Filial Conduct preface; of the biographies only Zhang Sheng's comes from Zong Jian's catalogue (see the Song note above); the other biographies wholly match the Northern History, and the discussion too is from the Northern History though slightly abridged.
translations.idiomatic: This biography's preface differs from the History of the Northern Dynasties juan 84 Filial Conduct preface. Of the biographies, only Zhang Sheng's comes from Zong Jian's catalogue (see the Song note above). The other biographies wholly match the Northern History, and the discussion too is drawn from the Northern History, though slightly abridged.

sentences.zh: 北史序中記魏書此卷傳目，全同今本，只張昇、倉跋先後互易。

translations.literal: The Northern History preface records this juan's biography list in the Book of Wei, wholly matching the present text, only Zhang Sheng and Cang Ba's order is reversed.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern History preface records this juan's biography list in the Book of Wei, wholly matching the present text, except that Zhang Sheng and Cang Ba are reversed in order.

sentences.zh: 從者於路偶得一羊 諸本及北史卷二四趙逸附趙琰傳「偶」都作「遇」，冊府卷七九三

translations.literal: Follower on the road happened to obtain a sheep: all editions and Northern History juan 24, Zhao Yi attached to Zhao Yan's biography, read "encountered" for "happened upon"; Ce fu yao lan juan 793
translations.idiomatic: Follower on the road happened to obtain a sheep: all editions and Northern History juan 24, Zhao Yi attached to Zhao Yan's biography, read "encountered" for "happened upon"; Ce fu yao lan juan 793

sentences.zh: 〈九四一二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 9412〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 9412〉

sentences.zh: 作「偶」。

translations.literal: reads "happened upon."
translations.idiomatic: reads "happened upon."

sentences.zh: 按文義作「偶」是，今據改。

translations.literal: By the sense of the text "happened upon" is correct; the text is emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: By the sense of the text "happened upon" is correct; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 出為鄯善鎮將 諸本及北史卷八四乞伏保傳「鄯善」作「無善」，通志卷一六七乞伏保傳倒作「善無」。

translations.literal: Posted as commandant of Shanshan garrison: all editions and Northern History juan 84, Qifu Bao biography, read "Wushan" for "Shanshan"; Tong zhi juan 167, Qifu Bao biography, inverts this to "Shanwu."
translations.idiomatic: Posted as commandant of Shanshan garrison: all editions and Northern History juan 84, Qifu Bao biography, read "Wushan" for "Shanshan"; Tong zhi juan 167, Qifu Bao biography, inverts this to "Shanwu."

sentences.zh: 按墓誌集釋有乞伏寶墓誌

translations.literal: According to Epitaph Collection and Explanation there is Qifu Bao's tomb epitaph
translations.idiomatic: According to Epitaph Collection and Explanation there is Qifu Bao's tomb epitaph

sentences.zh: 〈圖版二八四〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 284〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈plate 284〉

sentences.zh: ，即此乞伏保，誌稱「遷鄯善鎮將，以母憂解任」。

translations.literal: — this is the same Qifu Bao; the epitaph says "transferred to Shanshan garrison commandant, resigned on mother's mourning."
translations.idiomatic: — this is the same Qifu Bao. The epitaph says he was "transferred to commandant of Shanshan garrison and resigned on his mother's mourning."

sentences.zh: 鄯善鎮屢見本書。

translations.literal: Shanshan garrison appears repeatedly in this book.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan garrison appears repeatedly in this book.

sentences.zh: 元和郡縣志卷三九鄯州條云：「後魏以西平郡為鄯善鎮，孝昌二年，改鎮立鄯州。」

translations.literal: Yuanhe junxian zhi juan 39 Shanzhou entry says: "Later Wei made Xiping commandery the Shanshan garrison; in the second year of Xiaochang the garrison was changed and Shanzhou established."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe junxian zhi juan 39, Shanzhou entry, says: "Later Wei made Xiping commandery the Shanshan garrison. In the second year of Xiaochang the garrison was abolished and Shanzhou established."

sentences.zh: 這裏「鄯」字訛「無」，而恒州的善無郡

translations.literal: Here "Shan" in Shanshan is corrupted to "Wu," while the Shanshan commandery of Shanzhou
translations.idiomatic: Here "Shan" in Shanshan is corrupted to "Wu," while the Shanshan commandery of Shanzhou

sentences.zh: 〈見卷一０六上地形志上〉

translations.literal: 〈see Geography juan 106 upper〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈see Geography juan 106, part 1〉

sentences.zh: 人所習知，通志遂以為倒文，意為改乙，其實善無並未立鎮。

translations.literal: is well known to all; the Tong zhi therefore took it for inverted text and meant to emend—but in fact Shanshan never had a garrison established.
translations.idiomatic: is well known to all. The Tong zhi therefore took this for inverted text and meant to emend it—but in fact no garrison was ever established at Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 今據墓誌改。

translations.literal: Changed now according to the epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: The text is emended now according to the epitaph.

sentences.zh: 又墓誌記歷官較詳，保死在襄州刺史任上，非南中郎將。

translations.literal: Also the epitaph records offices in greater detail: Bao died in the post of regional inspector of Xiangzhou, not as Southern Palace General.
translations.idiomatic: The epitaph also records his offices in greater detail: Bao died while serving as regional inspector of Xiangzhou, not as Southern Palace General.
